summary:
Footprints in Space is a 7-slide PowerPoint that tells the story of NASA's hardware left across the solar system, written for school-age space fans. It moves outward from the Moon to Mars to deep space. Along the way it covers Apollo's rovers, laser reflectors and seismometers, the Mars rovers from Sojourner to Perseverance, the still-transmitting Voyagers, and quieter explorers like Pioneer 10, Cassini and New Horizons.
It meets the challenge by pairing each piece of hardware with what it is doing now (still working, silent, or deliberately retired) and with the science it made possible, such as evidence of ancient water on Mars and the edge of the Sun's bubble. Short text, icons and big numbers keep it approachable. Speaker notes support a presenter, and the final slide asks students to design their own mission.
details: The project is a 7-slide PowerPoint presentation that works as a guided tour from the Moon to Mars to deep space. Each slide has one message: Apollo's leftovers, the Mars rovers, the Voyagers, the quiet explorers, what we learned, and a closing challenge. Every piece of hardware gets the same three things: what it is, where it is now, and what it taught us. Speaker notes on each slide give a presenter talking points. Benefits and intended impact It turns a long history into short, memorable facts (for example, Opportunity was built for 90 days and worked for almost 14 years). It works for a live class talk or for students reading on their own. It aims to show that these machines are active legacies, and to spark curiosity about space careers. The last slide asks students to imagine their own mission.
